content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Outcome: deviation (not missing).** The planner hint predicted no insurance clause, but one exists — Section 14 at paragraph p0048, buried inside the Section 7 block rather than in its own section, which is why the outline didn't surface it. So this became a partial-coverage deviation and an in-place amendment rather than an insertion.

**What already complied:** workers' compensation at statutory levels, and certificates of insurance on request with notice of material change.

**Three gaps closed:**
1. CGL had a $1M limit with no aggregate → added $2M aggregate
2. E&O was $1M → raised to $2M
3. No cyber coverage at all → added $5M

The cyber gap was the substantive one. Two clauses confirmed the trigger: Section 1(c) contemplates Contractor personnel working at our facilities with access to Company computer systems, and Section 8 confirms Contractor obtains Company data, records and Confidential Information. A vendor with both premises access and data access carrying no cyber coverage sits at the playbook's walk-away line.

One drafting note worth flagging: the agreement defines no "Customer Data" term, so I couldn't use the model language verbatim. The cyber trigger is instead tied to "Company data or Confidential Information," leaning on the existing Section 8 definition to keep the hook enforceable within this document's own vocabulary.

I left two lower-value points alone to keep the edit proportionate at this severity: the "or self-insurance" language, which lets Contractor self-insure rather than carry real policies, and the clause's odd placement inside Section 7. If you want to press the self-insurance carve-out, that would be a separate ask. I did add the one-year post-term tail and "at its own expense," since E&O and cyber claims are usually made after an engagement ends and a term-only obligation would leave us exposed.
